Génération Do It Yourself — ou GDIY, mai: Génération Do It Yourself — or GDIY, but never "Génération DIY", the show's website insists — is Matthieu Stefani's interview podcast. Two Ts in Matthieu, one F in Stefani. He isn't a journalist: he's an entrepreneur, co-founder of the digital agency CosaVostra, who launched the show in 2017 and co-founded the label Orso Media in 2021 with Christofer Ciminelli. More than 570 episodes later, the slogan hasn't changed: "We are the average of the people we spend time with."
Le format tient en une ligne : un invité: The format fits in one line: one guest, about two hours. Childhood, struggles, fundraising, mistakes, figures, everything is covered. Guests range from CAC 40 CEOs to artists and athletes, sometimes with an original version and a French version when the guest is international. In June 2024, Stefani hosted Emmanuel Macron: a first for a sitting French president on a podcast.
Stefani ne dit jamais « racontez-nous vo: Stefani never says "tell us about your success". He asks how, how much, with whom, and what it cost when it failed. He gently digs to understand what drives people, without flattery, and he says when he likes something.
On ne prépare pas deux heures de pitch p: Nobody can rehearse a two-hour pitch. After a while, the guest relaxes, lowers their guard and drops the polished talking points. What looked like a gamble in 2017 has become a podcast classic: GDIY proved you can go long, demanding, and build a very large audience.
En quelques semaines : Eric Schmidt, anc: Within a few weeks: Eric Schmidt, former Google CEO, Veolia's chief executive on the water war, the head of Saint-Gobain, Virginie Taittinger on champagne, a criminal lawyer on "defending the indefensible". Business is the way into everything else.
Lolo, auditeur « attentionné » qui conna: Lolo, a "devoted" listener who knows the theme tune by heart, argued the case; Alex played the prosecutor, between two minutes devoted to money. Lolo's conclusion: Matthieu Stefani is the GOAT of podcasting. Nine years, a pace never dropped and still no short version — the lesson is above all one of consistency, and consistency remains the hardest part of the job. On the label side, we had already reviewed other Orso Media shows, like Tech 45' and If This Then Dev.
Trois limites et demie, pourtant. La lon: Three and a half limits, though. Length: two hours a week, impossible to keep up with everything, you have to pick. Survivorship bias: those who did the same thing and failed aren't in the chair, even if GDIY digs into failure better than most. And Stefani talks a lot: an anecdote about his butcher can land just as the guest was about to spill the beans. It's human, sometimes awkward, but it's a conversation, not an interrogation. And the half: he rarely seeks confrontation. You come out more admiring than challenged, and that's deliberate. Where to start: definitely not with the latest episode. Find someone you admire in the list, and give yourself the full two hours.
